fullText:
连线：黄仁勋重返英伟达后的首场全员大会：他究竟说了哪 11 句话？

1. 谈自我提升：“我每天都做足足一个半小时的心理治疗，这对我帮助非常大。”

2. 谈问责机制：“网上有些传言，说我显然就是个‘科技直男’ (tech bro)，所以才能回来；还说因为我是‘科技直男’，穿着一件特别酷的皮衣，就可以凌驾于法律和行为准则之上。这完全不是事实。这种事绝不会被容忍，在这里也从未被容忍过。”

3. “如果你们当中有人违反了行为准则，这意味着什么？如果你真的违反了，那肯定是不妥的。我只是想让你们明白：这是不对的、不妥的，也绝不会被容忍。但‘绝不容忍’，并不意味着你一违反准则，我们马上就把你扫地出门。我们得看事实、看具体情况，还要做大量评估。最终仍由你们的管理团队来做决定，综合所有事实与背景，做出最符合公司和员工利益的判断。”

4. 谈自己的管理风格：“我带来的那种高强度高压感，能把每个人都推向更高的水准。但有时我会做得太过火。一旦过火，就会伤害到别人，让他们感到被贬低、被剥夺了掌控感。这样做是不对的。所以我得好好琢磨，接下来该如何把这种强度，这种近乎疯狂的强度，带到工作当中。”

5. 谈英伟达的女性员工：“我认为我们必须为所有女性员工营造并持续维护一个安全的环境。如果我做过的任何事危及了这种安全感，我简直无法形容自己有多难过，我会竭尽全力去弥补。我们绝不容忍那种情况发生。”

6. 谈接班人与继任：“哪怕一整天不管，这家公司也能自动运转，你们都亲眼看到了。我向你们保证，无论我在还是不在，这家公司的基因里就刻着执行、执行、再执行，并交出亮眼的财务业绩。”

7. “我以前也不相信所谓的继任计划 (succession planning)。你们好好消化一下这句话，我不信继任计划，我觉得它有缺陷。倒不是‘继任’这个理念本身有缺陷，而是人们通常理解的那套继任计划有问题。”

8. “我们没有继任计划是有原因的，绝不是因为我们没听说过这个词。我是科技史上在任时间最长的 CEO。”

9. 谈政治：“还有传言说，我之所以能回来，是因为美国政府最高层希望我回来。这也完全是无稽之谈。我们的董事会只是履行了他们应尽的职责。”

10. “特朗普总统确实非常、非常喜欢我们公司，”黄仁勋对员工说，“他总爱拿英伟达出来炫耀，你们也都知道。但这就引出了一个关于政治的问题：我们现在变得政治化了吗？我们站队了吗？我想向你们明确表态：特朗普总统是美国总统，也是我的总统。我会竭尽所能，向这位总统提供必要的信息，帮助他做出最符合国家利益的决策……这是我们必须做的事。而无论下一任总统是谁，他都会是我的总统，我也同样会这么做。”

11. “一秒钟都不要以为政治在这家公司里起什么作用，哪怕一点点都没有。我们是最不沾染政治的公司。我不喜欢大家在这里谈论政治——想聊政治，带回家去聊。我喜欢大家在这里只谈工作。”

fullText:
Alibaba vs. Coke: Why Digital Growth Never Runs Dry

Chris Zook's Profit from the Core is really a good book about growth. It's one of my "go to" reads.

But the emergence on digital businesses really changes how to think about growth.

How does Alibaba grow versus a traditional business like Coca-Cola?

Here's my quick summary.

Note: I have a full podcast episode on this. Link below.

--

Point 1: In digital, growth by innovation is a bottomless well.

Coke will run out of new sodas, and Apple will run out of new countries.

But an app can keep adding features, bundles, touch points and personalization. 

Pretty much forever.

--

Point 2: Not all digital growth needs to be profitable.

Alibaba chases instant commerce for mindshare, delivering a sweater in 15 to 20 minutes, while barely making money.

But Alibaba also says it is increasing profits in its core ecommerce.

Growth can be in profits, users and / or engagement. All 3 matter.

--

Point 3: Growth is a weekly grind, not a rare big bet.

Growth initiatives in new products, channels and geographies succeed only about 25% of the time.

Going for one step adjacencies, like a digital service on a screen customers already use, raise the odds of success.

But it's something you practice all the time. 

--

***Takeaways for Managers:

1: Pick two or three growth ideas to test this month and review the numbers weekly.

I go deeper on this in Episode 259 of The Tech Strategy Podcast.

https://t.co/KVWnFSG6g7

QUESTION: Where does most of your growth come from today: the core, adjacencies or innovation?

fullText:
4 GenAI Lessons from Sangeet Choudary's Book Reshuffle

Is the biggest GenAI opportunity productivity or coordination?

Everyone is focused on productivity. For good reason. 

But strategist Sangeet Choudary argues the biggest opportunity is coordination.

Here's are my take-aways.

Note: There is more on this in my free weekly email, link below.

--

1: GenAI is a new technology for coordination, not just a productivity tool.

Nobel winner Ronald Coase said firms exist because they lower coordination costs, also called transaction costs.

Platform business models like Airbnb and Stripe lower those costs too, but only for interactions that can be standardized.

GenAI is able to lower coordination costs in non-standardized situations. Which is most things.

--

2: Like the shipping container, GenAI will hit tasks first, then organizations, then whole ecosystems.

Malcolm McLean commercialized the standard container in 1956, so cargo could move between ships, trucks and trains without unloading.

The bigger effect came later, when global trade opened up and companies no longer had to vertically integrate.

--

3: GenAI can coordinate messy ecosystems that platforms never could.

Online travel agencies like Expedia have long struggled to go beyond basic hotel and flight bookings.

Humans do the coordination between the various parts of a trip. 

However, GenAI can read all the reviews, handle unstructured data and plan taxis, food and experiences across many sites at once. For the whole trip.

--

***Takeaways for Managers:

1: Pick one messy process this week where your teams and suppliers still coordinate by email and meetings, and test a GenAI tool on it.

fullText:
Beyond Google Veo: I Asked Tencent WAND's Head of Product Why Specialized Video Models Are Better

I interviewed Yuna Fu, Head of Product for Tencent's WAND, about the new WAND-Vega model suite. 

***

Video generation is already widely used in ecommerce, media and enterprise. 

But performance vs. cost is still a challenge. 

Specifically, "prompt and pray" where you prompt and then spend a lot of compute generating a video. Hoping it works. 

If it doesn't, you try again.

That's where Tencent's new WAND Vega suite of models is trying to change the game. 

Vega lets you create intermediate models for editing. 

Basically, cheap low-res previews or drafts you can edit before the expensive full render.

***

Overall, Vega is betting that specialized video models will evolve to be better and cheaper than generalized models. 

Although it helps that WAND is being built in parallel with Tencent's Hy suite.

It also helps that Tencent is the largest gaming company in the world. With huge amounts of real video and graphics data.

***

Here's the suite:

- WAND-Vega-Video generates video.

- WAND-Vega-Image generates images.

- WAND-Vega-VL understands inputs. Important for summaries, product identification, performance reviews, and data labeling. 

- WAND-Vega-Audio handles audio, including speech recognition, subtitle extraction and translation, AI dubbing, voice separation and audio
